- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2 day lag in reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward correction of 3–7% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model is prone to volatility mispricing; use 1–2% smoothing filter to dampen extreme swings.
